Name: The MTI Group
Description:
Miceli Technologies Inc. (MTI) was founded in 1999 as a consulting firm to the manufacturing base in Windsor, Ontario, Canada. Our sole purpose was to help industry explore and adopt new technologies that could improve competitiveness through efficiencies in manufacturing methodologies and processes in the ever-growing global marketplace.
Much improvement was made in our customers productivity. However, time and again a bottleneck began to make itself apparently obvious. The issue was the average feed rate of their machine tools. No matter how new the machine or what options were installed on the control, machining complex geometry was painfully slow. When changes in direction occurred the machine’s feed rate dropped dramatically. An increase in controller memory and the use of “look ahead” technology did not improve the situation enough. It occurred to us that something needed to be done.

After several years of thorough analysis we came to the conclusion that the CNC controls on the market were not able to move machine tools anywhere close to their designed mechanical capabilities; the machines iron was capable of so much more. From this discovery, the MTI Constant Velocity Controller (CVC) was born.

In 2002 MTI turned all of it’s resources to bear on the task of re-thinking how CNC controllers were engineered. Input was gathered from all sectors of the industry. Ideas were tested and myths were disproved. Many prototypes were installed in the field and years of feedback was given from operators, managers and technicians.

The final result is an extremely robust and reliable CVC offering. The MTI controller accomplishes our initial goal of running a machine tool at an average feed rate that reflects the true capabilities of the iron it is attached to, while always respecting the machine tool’s intended design specifications.

The time for the adoption of new programs can be cut from weeks to a single day, enabling the automation of short-run production.

Since 1982, K+S has been repairing automation for industries such as Tire and Rubber, Mining, Aerospace, Food & Beverage, White Goods, Petrochemical, Paper & Pulp, Steel, Printing, Plastics, Automotive and Tier 1 Automotive to name a few. We specialize in electronic components such as PLC's, servo drive repair, robotics, servo motor repair, monitors, encoders, CNC systems, laser scanners, spindle repair, power supplies, operator panels, welder repair, weld controls and other electronic equipment. All of our repairs, whether a servo drive repair or welder repair, are rigorously tested using custom designed closed-loop system test stands and the latest diagnostic technologies to verify performance and functionality. Each repair is covered by our 12-month In-Service warranty. We verify, calibrate, and fully test the work performed to meet or exceed OEM specifications. Each item is sent back with a detailed repair report outlining what we found wrong with your component as well as the work performed and associated final testing. With 14 K+S Repair Operations ready to serve you world-wide, we are committed to demonstrating that K+S Services is the Leader in industrial electronic repair and Automation Repair Services. Name: PushCorp
Description:
PushCorp is the leading manufacturer of robotic material removal end-of-arm tooling. For over 30 years our products have helped customers automate applications that were once considered impossible to do with a robot. These include robotic grinding, robotic sanding, robotic deburring, robotic polishing, robotic milling, and many more. PushCorp's force compliant tooling gives a robot a “human” touch. Our active technology allows for accurate force to be maintained against a surface in any orientation. The equipment achieves this through proprietary algorithms that monitor force, position and acceleration in real time.

In addition to force compliance devices, PushCorp offers a wide range of powerful, efficient, and factory proven electric spindles. All of PushCorp's spindles utilize liquid cooled, permanent magnet, brushless, closed-loop servomotor technology. This technology gives our spindles the highest power-to-weight ratio and power efficiency in the industry.

Our 20,000 sqft, state of the art manufacturing facility located in Dallas, Texas houses engineering, sales, assembly labs, a full machine shop, and robotics labs. This has allowed us to bring 100 percent of our manufacturing and assembly in-house and given us the ability to produce high quality systems more efficiently than ever before. 

Adding to our engineering and manufacturing capabilities, we have three state of the art robotic labs dedicated to proof of concept testing. In these labs we take pre-processed parts and, through testing, determine the best PushCorp equipment and abrasives to achieve customer's required processing goals. As a result, these proof-of-concept demonstrations significantly de-risk projects for both system integrators and end users. 

Supplementing our headquarters, we have sales offices in Wixom, Michigan and Montreal, Canada. With their central location, we are able to provide close local support for the regions.

Description:
Innovators of proprietary nodeCLOUD Rapid 3D scanning of full-sized human models with subsequent rapid large-format printing of hyper-realistic life-sized human mannequin hard shells and soft shells using our proprietary One-Shot textureFLOOD 3D Printing technology.

Our developers  spent years creating a full-body 3D scanner for human models and transforming the resulting 3D image of the living person into synthetic creations so life-like they could easily be mistaken for real people. 

We named this scanning method nodeCLOUD. 

Think of it like a digital sandbox in which the spatial location of every single grain of sand is digitized ON or OFF. If the grain is set to ON, then it occupies its position (or NODE) in the sandbox. If you set the grain to OFF it leaves its position and gets digitally transported to a repository or holding cell.

Next, put billions  of these digital grains into a virtual sandbox with an open top. Network the digital location of each grain (or "node") so you could turn each one ON or OFF from a master controller, and you have the basic concept behind the adamsBiONiCS nodeCLOUD Full-Body 3D Scanner.

Now plunge your hand into the sandbox.

If it were real beach sand in a wooden box the grains of sand would be displaced from the space that your hand occupies and the sand would overflow and spill out of the box. The same thing happens in the nodeCLOUD except that rather than digital grains getting displaced they simply disappear from the nodeCLOUD – or get digitally transported – and reappear in a repository we named the nodeBIN. All the other grains that are not displaced by your hand remain exactly where they are in the nodeCLOUD. The resulting 3D digital image of your hand in the  nodeBIN is then transformed into a solid "real" 3-dimensional body by coating the image with an "sticky" binder then flooding the nodeBin with an elastomeric resin such as silicone.	Somewhat like dumping a bucket of flour onto a person coated with molasses.
